detail.classification: agent by capability, not by judgment: the work is verbatim transport execution of queued bridge records (chat_send, chat_list, chat_tail, permissions_list) under bodies/bridge-wake-item.md, and only an agent holds the runtime tools those verbs execute through - the classification test fails on kind, not on discretion, since the body forbids judgment outright (never widen a send, never alter queued text, never approve or deny). The executing runtime matters as much as the kind: worker-class runtimes hold only the read half of the chat namespace (no send function even after the namespace loads), so the minter addresses the escalation ping to the drain home thread (the owners config drain mapping - a full agent surface whose send capability the F5 proof drain exercised), and a worker that encounters this ping leaves it for that surface. Wakes: primarily the bridge-wake minter episode escalation ping (job bridge-drain, planted once per non-empty queue episode); the hourly cadence is a backstop sweep for anything the escalation missed, and a backstop wake that finds an empty queue acks and ends. The executor acks the escalation ping only when its final poll finds the queue empty - that ack is the episode close the minter re-arms on.
detail.title: Bridge drain executor — works the connector bridge queue under its per-item contract

detail.classification: fixed command (one Python script): each pass reads the connector bridge queue from its record files and plants one wake ping per queued item in the scheduler outbox through the server own Outbox class - the per-item programmatic generation half of the bridge drain re-host (plan 2026-11-10). Wake addressing is derived, never judged: a chat_send wake targets the record own args.chat_id; a read tool (chat_list, chat_tail, permissions_list) targets the requesting caller owning thread from bodies/bridge-wake-owners.yaml. Every outcome is enumerable in advance: WAKE (a ping minted; quiet pattern), DRAIN (an episode escalation ping for the bridge-drain agent job minted; quiet pattern), silence (queue empty or every item already has a pending wake), or UNRESOLVED (an item with no resolvable target - left queued and reported, never guessed). Episode escalation (F5 home, 2026-11-11): a pass finding at least one resolvable queued item and no pending bridge-drain ping plants that ping once (detail: the resolvable count, plus target_chat from the owners config drain mapping when configured - the escalation is addressed to the drain home thread, a full agent surface carrying the chat send function, because worker-class runtimes hold only the read half of the chat namespace and an unaddressed drain ping claimed by one stalls every chat_send item; defect diagnosed 2026-11-12 after two such stalls); the executor acks it only when its final poll finds the queue empty, so a standing bridge-drain ping is the open episode and the first pass after its ack re-mints - no minter state, the outbox is the record. An unresolved-only queue never escalates. The ping detail carries the item identity and destination only, never its text; minting approves nothing and executes nothing - execution stays with the woken executor under the bridge contract (tools, never authority). Idempotence is the outbox itself: one pending ping per item job id, terminal records never re-minted, an acked-but-unfulfilled item re-minted on the next pass.
detail.title: Bridge wake minter - one thread-addressed wake ping per queued connector bridge item

detail.classification: fixed command (one Python script): every pass reads the boot identity (the restart detector's /proc source) and evaluates the live manifest (registry/file-registry.yaml) exactly per the file-registry contract v1 — presence rules exists / non-empty / sha256 with no partial credit, restore by declared class only (tracked from the repo HEAD, generated by the declared generator, backup copied back — a backup that fails presence flags rather than chaining; flag-only never written), every restore re-checked, an unrestorable failure flagged with its entry's owner named. Speaking is fully determined: one findings-first report when findings exist and the boot changed or the findings differ from the last reported set, silence on a clean or unchanged pass, exit 3 when the manifest or boot-id source is unreadable or invalid. detail.classification: fixed command (one Python script): every cycle runs the flap canary (ops/flap_canary.py) from two spawning origins — a plain server-tree child (control) and a child placed before exec into a dedicated /sys/fs/cgroup/init.scope/hatch-tool-prepared-flapwatch cgroup, mimicking the agent tool layer origin that the write-denial flap denies. Per-arm verdicts append to state/flap-watch-series.jsonl; output (and so a report) happens only on an arm transition, baseline adoption silent — the boot-detector shape. This entry is an ARMED EXPERIMENT, not a settled detector: between waves both origins write fine, so a clear cgroup-arm reading is inconclusive until a live wave tests it against agent-class ground truth (ops/flap_probe.py from an agent shell). Pre-stated criteria and the ground-truth protocol: state/flap-probe-study/read-signal-hunt.md. If the cgroup arm tracks the agent class across one full wave (denied at the start, clear at the clear, control clear throughout), the mimicry holds and this scripted entry is the flap job. If it stays clear while agent-class writes are denied through a full wave, mimicry fails: this entry is removed and an agent-cadence entry is admitted with that negative result in its classification evidence — the experiment outcome decides the final kind.
detail.title: Flap watcher — origin-mimicry experiment, scripted detection of write-denial waves

detail.classification: fixed command (one Python script): every cycle samples processes via /proc (argv + cwd + pid/ppid, reads only) and branches on the mechanical matchers alone, in two modes chosen by a mechanical signal — whether any colab-liveness entry stands in the registry (a live High-RAM fleet session; the lease core renders and removes those entries). NORMAL mode (no fleet live): silence when no test-runner process has its cwd inside the workspace; one LOCAL-TEST finding line per new episode per process signature (episode state in state/local-test-watch.json; a continuing episode never re-speaks, a closed episode that reappears is a new finding); the narrow pre-check exemption is mechanical (one test file plus a name filter; pytest <=5 named node ids from one file, or one file plus -k); check.py and package-test always flag. STRICT mode (fleet live; owner ruling 2026-11-10): the exemption is suspended and the trigger broadens to any local check/code execution from a workspace repo — test runners and gates, dev/backend servers (server binaries, python -m http.server, server-shaped script names, package dev/serve/start scripts), and experiment scripts (an interpreter running a script file) — while managed infrastructure never flags (the scheduler system's own automation surface — any argv running a script under this repo's ops/ or bin/, the scripted legs and this watcher included — and argv matching the untracked routes file's service patterns: the long-running servers, the fleet machinery; ancestry is not the discriminator, since agent work routed through the server's ops channel runs as server children too and must still flag). A strict finding is a WARNING printed on first sighting in the same cycle, naming the repo's owning thread from the untracked routes file, and is also sent directly to that thread via the harness connector (caller local-test-watch, send scope, envelope local-test-watch-<signature> for dedupe) when a route and token are configured; the printed line reaches the main chat as the sweeper's copy, so no finding waits on downstream classification. Exit 3 when /proc cannot be listed. Flagging is on sight, never load-gated; the load average is recorded in the finding as context only. Speaking is fully determined by those branches; the watcher reports and routes facts and judges nothing beyond the mechanical matchers.
detail.title: Local test watcher — deterministic detection of test runs on the local box

On new orphans it plants one addressed outbox ping per resolved owning thread (caller -> chat from bodies/restart-reconcile-owners.yaml, exact caller then caller namespace — the segment before its first colon — then dash-family prefix; unresolved callers are never guessed and print as UNRESOLVED) and prints one summary; a record reports once per episode (episode state in state/restart-reconcile.json), closes silently when its record reaches a terminal state, and re-reports under a new boot.
